SUMMARY
An altitude-wind-tunnel investigation has been made to deter-
mine the performance of a Curtiss 836-14C2-18R1 four-blade propel-
ler on a YP-47M airplane at high blade loadings and high engine
powers. The atudy waa made for a range of power coefficients from
0.10 to 1.00 at free-satream Mach numbers of 0.30, 0.40, and 0.50,
The results of the force measurements indicate primarily the trend
of propeller efficiency for changes in power coefficient or
edvance-diemeter ratio, inasmuch asp no corrections for the effecta
of tunnel-well constriction on the installation were applied.
Siipstream surveys are presented td illustrate blade thrust load
. otstribubion for several operating conditions.
.For the range. of advencé-diameter ratios investigated at a
free-stream Mach number of 0. 30, highest efficiencies were obtained
at vower, coefficients from 0.10 to 0.30 and flow breakdown was
evident for power coefficients’ above 0.40.
“The maximum efficiencies at’ a’ free-atream:Mach number of 0.40
were, obtained for power coefficients from 0.20 to 0,40, between
advance-diameter ratios of P.50 anil 3.10. The envelope of the
efficiency curves decreased about 15 percent between advance-
diameter ratios of. 2. 20 and 3.80. °°

INTRODUCTION .
An investigation of the performanca of several propellers on
the YP-47M airplane at. high blade loadings has been conducted in
the Cleveland altitude wind tunnel at the request of the Air Materiel
Command, Army Air Forces. As pert of the program, a study was made
of a Curtiss 836-14C2-18R1. four-blade propeller.
The investigation was made for a range of power coefficients
from 0.10 to 1.00 at free-stream Mach numbers of 0.30, 0.40, ard 0.50
for density altitudes from 10,000 to 45,000 feet, engine powers from
150 to 2500 brake horsepower, and for engine speeds fram 1000 to
2900 xm. -
The propeller efficiencies were obtained from force measurements
and the blade thrust load distribution was obtained by two diamet-
rically opposed slipatream survey rakes as in references 1 to 4,

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
The resulta of the force measurements are primarily of value
in showing the trend of propeller efficiency for changes in power
coefficient or advance-diemeter ratio. The absolute efficiency
values are questionable because an average drag coefficient for the
installation was used for all the propellers investigated. Data
obtained at different free-stream Mach numbers are not comparable
because corrections for tunneli-wall constriction effecta, which vary
with airspeed, have not been applied. (See reference 1.) Slip-
stream surveys are presented to illustrate the blade thrust load
distribution for several operating conditions. :
Free-stream Mach number, 0.30. - The effect of advance-diameter
ratto on tne propeller efficiency at a free-stream Mach number of
0.50 is shown in figure 4 for a renge of power coefficients from
: 0,10 to 1.00. The variation of propeller efficiency with power
coefficient is shown in figure 5 for approximately constant values
of advance-diameter ratio. For the range of advance-diameter ratios
investigated, highest efficiencies were obtained at power coerfi-
cients from 0.10 to 0.30. In general, large reductions in effi-
clency due ta Piow breakdown were evident at power coefficients
above 9.40. (See figs. 4 and 5.)
The effect cf power coefficient on the blade thrust loed dis-
tribution is shown by the siipstream surveys in figure-6, which
correspond to the conditiona of figure 5 for d#1.00. The blade

the blede span for a power coefficient of 0.10. (See fig. 6(a).)

change in power coefficient from 0.30 to 0,40. The maximum load
however, shifted inboard to (r,g/R)* = 0,50, indicating that flow
breakdown occurred on the tip sectiona. (See fig. 6(a4)}.) Thies

The difference between the right and the ieft surveys was

The effect of advance-diameter ratio on the blade thrust load
distribution is shown by slipstream surveys in figures 7 and 8,
which correspond to the conditions of figure 4, for power coeffi-

0.20, a reduction in advance-diameter ratio from 2.00 to 1.52

ably. When the advance-diameter ratio was decreased from 1,32 to
1.00 (figs. 7(c) and 7(d)) there was a reduction in over-all thrust;
however, this reduction in thrust loading was due to the higher

of 1.00 was obtained, At a power coefficient of 0.40 (fig. 8),a4
change in advance-diameter ratio from 2.04 to 1.16 resulted ina
more rapid increase of thrust loading on’ the outboard sections than
on the inboard sections. <A further change in advance-diameter ratio
from 1.16 to 1,01 increased the over-all thruat loading, and flow

0.10 to 1,00. The variation af prupeller efficiency with power
coefficient is shown In figvre 10 for approximately constant values

Hishest efficiencies were obtained at power coefficients from
0.20 to 0.40 at advance-diameter ratios from 1.50 to 3.10. ‘The
envelope of the efficiency curves decreased about 15 percent between
advance-diameter ratios of 2.20 and 3.80. (See fig. 9.) As the
power coefficient wes increased, the peak efficiency occurred at
generally increasing values of advance-diamseter ratio, In the low

to blade stall were evident at the nigh power coefficients, For
xample, at an advance-diameter ratio of 1.70, a change in power
coefficient from 0.60 to 0.70 resulted in a 24-percent reduction in
propeller efficiency. ;
The effect of power coefficient on blade thruat load distri-
bution is shown by the slipstream surveys in figure 11, which corre-

0,60, and the maximum loading occurred on sections at about
(rg/R)® = 0.70, (See figs. 11(a) to 11(e).) Blade stall was evi-
dent at power coefficients of 0.71 and 0.92. (See figs. 11(f)
and il(g).) The magnitudes of the thrust loadings shown in fig-
ure 11 cannot be compared, inasmuch as the surveys were obtained at
different density altitudes.

SUMMARY OF RESULTS
Because correctiong for twunnel-wall constriction have not been
applied, the propeller efficiencies presented in this report are
useful primarily in showing the comparative effects of blade loading
on propeller performance. The investigation in the altitude wind
tunnel of the performance at high blade loadings of a Curtiss
836-14C2-18R1 four-blade propeller on a YP-47M airplane indicated
that:
1. For the rangé of advance-diameter ratios investigated at a
free-stream Mach number of 0.30, highest efficiencies were obtained
at power coefficients from 0.10 to 0.30 and flow breakdown was
evident for power coefficients above 0.40.

NACA RM No, E631 . 9
2. Highest efficiencies at a free-stream Mach number of 0.40
were obtained for power coefficients from 0.20 to 0.40 at advance-
dieneter ratios from 1.50 to 3.10. The envelope of efficiency
curves decreased about 15 percent between advance-diameter ratios
of 2.20 and 3.80.
3. At a free-stream Mach number of 0.50, maxima efficiency in
the low range of advance-diameter ratios was obtained for a power
coefficient of 0.50, and in the high range of advance-diameter
ratios at a power coefficient of 1.00. The envelope of the effi-
cLlency curves decreased about 4 percent between advance-diameter
ratios of 2.20 and 3.60.
4. In general, velow the stall the local thrust loading was a
maximum on the tip sections at the low advance-diameter ratios and
& maximum on the inboard sections at the high advence-diameter
ratios. As stall developed at the blade tips the maximum thrust
loading shifted toward the inboard sections of the blades.
